UTTARA KANDA 
Recognizing his people's profound attachment, Rama 
answered, " So be it ! " and occupied himself in carrying through 
what he had undertaken that day. 
He gave over the Southern Koshalas to the valiant Kusha and 
those of the north to Lava ; thereafter, placing those two princes 
on his lap, he enthroned them in Ayodhya and bestowed upon 
them thousands of chariots and numberless elephants with ten 
thousand horses. 
Having furnished them with jewels and 
treasure in abundance and given them cheerful and healthy 
people to attend upon them, he sent the two brothers, Kusha 
and Lava, each to his own capital. 
Those two heroes being installed in their respective cities, 
Rama sent out an emissarv to the magnanimous ShatruJdma. 
CHAPTER 108 
Rama issues his last Comnuznds 
THE messengers, urged on by Rama's command, swiftly and 
promptly went to Madhura without halting on the way. After 
three nights they reached that city where they all informed 
Shattughna what had happened ; the banishing of Lakshmana, 
Raghava's vow, the installation of his two sons and the resolution 
of his subjects to follow him ; how an enchanting city had been 
built for Kusha under the name of Kushavati on the high ridge 
of the Vindhya Mountains by the virtuous Rama, and that 
Shravasti was the name of the ravishing and famous capital of 
Lava ; they told him also of the preparations made by Raghava 
and Bharata to take all the people from Ayodhya and enter 
Svarga. 
Having related all these things to the magnanimous Shattugh-
na, the messengers became silent and thereafter added, " Make 
all haste, 0 King I " 
Heating these fearful tidings regarding the imminent destruc-
tion of his entire House, Shattughna, the Joy of Raghu, called 
his people together and summoned his family priest, Kanchana, 
in order to impart the ttuth to them of his immediate departUte 
with his brothers.

Thereafter, that valiant prince installed his two sons, having 
distributed abundant wealth equally amongst them, and Subabu 
was established in Madhura and Shatrughatin in Vaidiaha. 
This being accomplished, that descendant of Raghu left for 
Ayodhya in a single chariot. 
There he beheld the magnanimous Rama like unto a flaming 
brazier, clothed in a robe of fine wool, in the midst of the im-
perishable Sages. Paying obeisance to them with joined palms, 
his senses under control, he addressed hia virtuous brother, 
whose thought too was ever fixed on his ducy, and said :-
" I have enthroned my two sons, 0 King, and have come 
hither ; know well that I am resolved to follow thee ! Do not 
oppose me, 0 Valiant One, for I would not that thy will should 
be disregarded by one like me." 
Seeing hia resolve was fixed, Rama said to Shattughna, " So 
be it." 
Having ceased from speaking, the monkeys, who were able to 
change their form at wiU, with the companies of bears and titans 
came there from all directions with Sugriva at their head, all 
being united in their desire to behold Rama, who stood with his 
face turned towards the sky. 
Devas, Rishia and Gandharvas with their offspring, hearing of 
Rama's intended departure, had all assembled, saying :-
" We have come here to follow thee, 0 Prince ! To leave with-
out us, 0 Rama is to strike us down with the Rod of Death." 
At that instant, the supremely powerful Sugriva, bowing 
before that hero in accord with tradition, addressed him with 
humilitY and said :-
" Having installed the virtuous Angada, 0 Prince, know that 
I have come hither with the intention of accompanying thee ! " 
At these words, the illustrious Kakutstha smiling, answered :-
" So be it ! " Thereafter be said to Bibiahana, the King of 
the Rakshasas :-
"As long as people exist, 0 Mighcy Lord of the Rakshasas, do 
thou remain in Lanka. As long as the moon and sun continue 
to shine on the eanh, as long as they speak of me in the world, so 
long shall thine empire endure ; this is the wiU of thy friend, do 
thou obey ! Govern thy people according to justice and do 
not question this further. One thing more I wish to say to thee,

brief.summary_1line: Rama finalizes succession, summons Shatrughna, and grants last commands as allies and beings gather to accompany him before his departure.

image_candidates.scene_text: Rama seats the young princes Kusha and Lava on his lap before enthroning them and sending them to rule their new capitals.
Shatrughna arrives in Ayodhya and sees Rama shining like a flaming brazier among assembled sages.
Hosts of monkeys, bears, gods, and sages gather around Rama as he stands facing the sky before his final departure.

deep.rich_summary: As Rama prepares for his final departure from the world, he first secures the future of his kingdom and lineage. He divides Kosala between his sons, installing Kusha in Kushavati in the Vindhya region and Lava in the famed city of Shravasti, giving them wealth, armies, and loyal subjects. Messengers then bring grave news to Shatrughna: Lakshmana’s banishment, Rama’s vow, and the people’s determination to follow their king into heaven. Realizing the end of their royal house on earth is near, Shatrughna enthrones his own sons and hastens to Ayodhya. There he finds Rama surrounded by sages and celestial beings who have gathered to witness his departure. Allies from across the epic—monkeys, bears, rakshasas, and gods—assemble, while Sugriva declares his intention to follow Rama, marking the beginning of a cosmic farewell to the avatar-king.

highlight_spans.why: Rama acknowledges the devotion of his people and begins the final actions that will close his earthly reign.
The symbolic transfer of power as Rama installs Kusha and Lava with wealth, armies, and authority.
The messengers reveal the alarming news to Shatrughna, signaling the impending end of Rama’s earthly house.
Shatrughna meets Rama in Ayodhya and declares his unwavering resolve to follow his brother.
A mythic gathering occurs as monkeys, bears, titans, sages, and celestial beings assemble to witness Rama’s departure.

top_scenes.scene_text: Rama stands radiant like a flaming brazier among assembled sages while armies of monkeys, bears, and celestial beings gather beneath the sky to witness his final departure.
Shatrughna arrives in Ayodhya and bows before Rama, who stands calm and luminous in woolen robes surrounded by immortal rishis.
Sugriva, with hosts of shape‑shifting monkeys and allied beings, approaches Rama from all directions as the world gathers for the king’s last journey.
